26D: 23 former opt-ins now standard, plus HCM pages switching to Redwood

26D is the current Oracle Fusion Cloud quarterly update, and it's rolling out now. Oracle updates environments by cohort: Cohort A gets 26D in November, Cohort B in December and Cohort C in January. Your own dates are in the Oracle Cloud Console.

This is also the first Fusion Updates briefing sent by email. By our count, Oracle's 26D What's New documents for Financials, Procurement, Supply Chain, Logistics, Projects and HCM list 789 features. Oracle hasn't published its 26D documents for Transportation Management, Global Trade Management or Work Life yet, so those aren't in the count, and Logistics means Warehouse Management only for now.

Below are the 8 changes I'd look at first, the former opt-ins that are now standard, the HCM pages switching to Redwood, and what to check. Everything links to Oracle's own page, so you can check the details for your setup.

23
former opt-ins now standard across all Fusion modules

The former opt-in count is Oracle's own Current Opt-In Expirations list. The other two are our tally: the Fusion Updates 26D tracker follows the most relevant changes, up to 25 per module family, out of the 789 features. Data from our 9 Nov 2026 weekly refresh.

The 8 changes I'd look at first

Across modules, in no particular order. Feature names are Oracle's.

Financials
1. Payables Period Close Workspace
A new workspace for the Payables close. For the selected ledger and period it brings together invoice, payment and period statuses, groups the exceptions that hold up the close, and walks your team through opening the next period, sweeping eligible unaccounted transactions and closing the current one, with Ask Oracle for questions in context. Oracle says there's nothing to enable, but users need the Payables Period Close Duty role, and the recommendations follow the close rules you configure. Decide who gets the role and review those rules before your next close.
Oracle source →
Procurement
2. Handle date changes in contract lines as inline updates in purchase agreements
The Import Purchase Agreements from External Purchase Prices process now updates the existing blanket purchase agreement line when a contract line's start or end date changes. Before, it end-dated that line and created a new one. Supported changes such as price, vendor part number and description can also be applied in place. It's on automatically, so if reports, integrations or mappings expect a new agreement line for each date change, check them.
Oracle source →
Time and Labor
3. Enhancements for Absence Integration on Redwood Time Cards
Removing an absence from a Redwood time card now deletes or withdraws it depending on its status, and applies your approval rules. After editing or removing a submitted or approved absence, workers can't just save the time card; they have to submit it. An absence that is part of an in-progress time card approval is read-only in Absence Management. It's on automatically, so tell workers and approvers, and test your approval rules.
Oracle source →
Payroll
4. Redwood Experience for Payroll Setup Pages
Six more Payroll setup pages open in Redwood, with their profile options set to Y by default: Balance Exceptions, Balance Exceptions and Reports, Element Security Profiles, Features by Country or Territory, Organization Payment Methods and Run Types. If a custom job role gives access to Organization Payment Methods, Oracle says it must include both the Organization Payment Method Management Duty role and the Manage Organization Payment Method privilege. Check your custom roles before your payroll team needs that page.
Oracle source →
Maintenance
5. Associate a technician to multiple labor resources
A technician can now be set up as more than one labor resource in an organization, for example as both a Mechanic and an Electrician. Advanced scheduling, Maintenance Supervision, My Maintenance Work and work reporting all take the extra skills into account. It's on automatically, and Oracle rates it larger scale. Agree how you'll model multi-skilled technicians before anyone sets them up, because it affects scheduling and labor costing.
Oracle source →
Manufacturing
6. Quality Assurance Workspace
Quality teams get one workspace to review recent work-in-process inspection results, Statistical Process Control (SPC) charts and rule-based signals such as Nelson Rule violations, with AI-assisted root cause insights and recommended actions. It's on automatically for users whose roles already have the inspection privileges Oracle lists. Oracle notes that SPC analysis needs at least 25 data points to be useful. It appears in both the Manufacturing and the Product Lifecycle Management What's New.
Oracle source →
Warehouse Management
7. Enhanced configuration migration safeguards and lock code handling
Before you import or copy configuration into a facility or company, WMS now backs up the matching destination records, and stops if the backup fails. In 3PL setups, lock codes can no longer be imported or copied into a child company, and facility-specific lock codes take the destination facility. If you ever need a backup file, Oracle says you have to raise a Service Request. Try your usual configuration migration in a test environment first.
Oracle source →
Project Management
8. Additional accounting sources for non-project labor costs
Labor Distribution now offers more worker assignment attributes for Subledger Accounting rules on non-project labor costs: assignment category and location, worker type, position, job, worker category, people group and assignment descriptive flexfields. It's on automatically. The new sources only matter once your accounting rules use them, so it's worth a look if you derive the natural account for labor costs outside projects.
Oracle source →

Former opt-ins that are now standard in 26D

Oracle's Current Opt-In Expirations list names 23 features whose opt-in period ends with 26D. They're now standard features. Oracle's "Now Enabled" column says Yes for 9 of them, so they're on for everyone; the other 14 need setup if you want to use them. If you already opted in and finished the setup, Oracle says there's nothing more to do.

19 of the 23 are in Financials, Projects, Procurement and Supply Chain: 14 in Supply Chain & Manufacturing (7 Manufacturing, 3 Inventory Management, 2 Maintenance, 1 Advanced Inventory Management, 1 Order Management), 3 in Projects, 1 in Procurement and 1 in Financials. 7 of these 19 are on for everyone and 12 need setup. The other 4 are 2 in Permitting and Licensing and 2 in Sales. The ones I'd look at first:

Manage Global Maintenance Work Definitions (Maintenance)
Now enabled, and Oracle rates it large scale. Work definitions with the same scope can be managed once in a maintenance-enabled master organization and replicated to child organizations. It's only in the Redwood Work Definitions page.

Redwood: Manage Global Work Definitions in an Item Master Organization (Manufacturing)
Now enabled, also large scale. A global work definition in the item master organization is assigned to child plants by the Propagate Global Work Definitions scheduled process, and the replicated copies are read-only apart from a few attributes. Redwood only.

Redwood: Set Up Customer Pricing (Order Management)
Now enabled, large scale. A Customer Pricing page in Pricing Administration lets you set pricing for a customer, an account or a group of customers.

Use Source Document as Transfer Price Basis for Orders in Back-to-Back Intercompany Transfers (Inventory Management)
Now enabled, small scale. Transfer prices for back-to-back internal transfers can come from the originating sales order price, with an optional markup or markdown. Oracle notes that once an active financial flow uses this option, you can't change it without creating a new financial flow agreement.

Redwood: Set up Supplier Registration and Profile Change Request (Procurement)
Needs setup if you want to use it. Redwood setup pages for supplier registration and for which supplier profile changes need approval.

All 23, with Oracle's columns →

HCM: pages switching to Redwood in 26D

HCM changes aren't on Oracle's opt-in expiration list, so they're not in the 23 above. Oracle announces them in its HCM What's New documents. For 26D, four announcements switch 34 pages to Redwood by default. You can still set each profile option back to No to keep the older page for now.

Person pages (6)
Personal Details, Contact Info, Identification Info, Family and Emergency Contacts, Additional Person Info and Person Identifiers for External Applications. Oracle moved this switch from 26C to 26D. If you set a profile option back to No in a test environment, Oracle says that setting is kept when the environment gets 26D, and each environment is evaluated on its own, so check production too.
Oracle source

Employment pages (21)
They include Hire an Employee, Promote, Transfer, Change Assignment, Change Manager and Work Relationship.
Oracle source

Workforce structures pages (5)
Departments, Enterprise HCM Information, Grade Ladders, Jobs and Locations.
Oracle source

Compensation (2)
My Compensation and Compensation Info. To keep the older pages, set the site-level profile option ORA_CMP_SPOTLIGHT_REDWOOD_ENABLED to No.
Oracle source

Other HCM changes in 26D

  • Journeys: You can no longer create journey tasks with the Process Automation task type. Oracle Process Automation reaches end of life on 31 October 2026. Oracle source
  • Payroll: The Create Time Card Calculation Component flow is retired. Elements already upgraded with it keep working but get no future enhancements, and Oracle suggests reimplementing them as Timecard-category elements. Oracle source
  • Learning: If the new Recommendations framework (available since 25A) isn't enabled before you get 26D, recommendations no longer appear in Oracle Learning. Oracle source
  • Learning: The responsive Career Development pages are no longer supported after 26D. Anyone still using them is moved to the Redwood experience automatically in 27A. Oracle source
  • Recruiting: From November 2026, Oracle no longer supports Digital Assistant Fusion Apps templates. Only career sites that already had the Digital Assistant Site Editor setting turned on keep it for now. Oracle recommends the Career Coach AI agent instead. Oracle source

Already announced for later

  • 27A: Resign From Employment, Terminate Employment and Mass Assignment Change switch to Redwood by default. The Redwood Mass Assignment Change page itself arrives in 26D. Oracle source
  • 27A: The Positions pages and the Request a New Position and Request a Position Change guided processes switch to Redwood by default. Oracle source
  • 27A: Customers using the Connections horizontal view are upgraded automatically to the waterfall view. Oracle source
  • 27B: Non-Redwood navigation to the older person pages (tiles, quick actions and navigator entries under My Client Groups, Person Management, Person Spotlight, Me, Directory, My Public Info and My Organization Chart) is disabled by default. Oracle source

All HCM Redwood switches and notices by release →

What to check now that 26D is here

  • Confirm your existing setup still works as before. Switch on new features as a separate change, not alongside these checks.
  • Check your key end-to-end flows by role: procure-to-pay, order-to-cash, plan-to-produce, hire-to-retire.
  • Re-run integrations: REST and SOAP calls, FBDI and HDL imports, B2B messages, and third-party systems.
  • Check critical reports (BI Publisher, OTBI) and any custom workflows and approvals.
  • Look at security: custom roles on new or changed Redwood pages, such as Organization Payment Methods in Payroll, and who should get the Payables Period Close Duty role.
  • In HCM, decide page by page whether you move to Redwood now or set the profile option back to No for a while, and check that setting in every environment.
  • Go through the 9 former opt-ins that are now on for everyone, and Oracle's "IMPORTANT Actions and Considerations" for each product you use.
  • Compare performance of your key flows with how they ran before the update.
